audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam (E) is not mentioned anywhere in either layer — not in the spikes, the whys, early, mid, late, the cooldown list, the dos or the donts.
audit.why: It is the ability that decides the matchup. Ground Slam reduces attack speed on a flat 7s cooldown, and Teemo's entire damage output is attack-speed-driven on-hit poison. Malphite has a hard answer to Toxic Shot available from level 3 and the guide never tells the player it exists. Its damage also scales with Malphite's Armor, so every armour item he buys makes it hit harder.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam: 7s flat, 400 range, cuts your attack speed and scales its damage off his own Armor. It is the reason extended trades go badly, and the reason his defensive items are also offensive ones.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (E Ground Slam, cd 7, range 400: 'deals magic damage based on his Armor and reduces the Attack Speed of enemies')

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry contradicts itself on armour and then gets it wrong in both directions. whys[2] says 'his armor stacking begins to blunt your E damage' and wants.foe[1] says he should 'stack armor items like Iceborn Gauntlet to reduce your E poison's relative value'. Toxic Shot is magic damage — armour does not reduce it at all. Elsewhere the entry correctly says the poison bypasses armour, so the two halves disagree.
audit.why: The player is told to fear an armour stack that cannot touch his damage, and is not told about the thing that armour DOES do here, which is make Ground Slam bigger.
audit.corrected: Armour is irrelevant to your poison because your poison is magic. What his armour actually buys him is Ground Slam damage, since Ground Slam scales off it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (E Toxic Shot — magic damage on-hit poison)
champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (E Ground Slam scales with Armor)

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard is described only as a slow ('his Seismic Shard Q slows you and keeps you in range'). It steals move speed for 3 seconds — you lose it and he gains it.
audit.why: Move Quick is Teemo's only disengage. Against a slow you are still moving away slowly; against a steal he is closing while you crawl, and the two effects are not interchangeable. It is also the exact 3-second window his ultimate is designed to follow.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard steals your move speed for 3s from 625 range. Getting hit by it is what makes Unstoppable Force lethal, not the ultimate's own range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (Q Seismic Shard, range 625: 'stealing Move Speed for 3 seconds')

audit.whatIsWrong: Thunderclap is called an 'armor aura' twice ('walking into his W armor aura', 'his W gives him bonus armor and a strong auto').
audit.why: Thunderclap is an attack reset that makes his following attacks throw aftershocks in front of him and shields him. It is an on-hit effect, which is precisely why blind is worth spending on it — an aura would not be blindable at all, so the mislabel hides the counterplay.
audit.corrected: Thunderclap is an attack reset with on-hit aftershocks. Blind eats the attacks it is loaded into.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (W Thunderclap; flags autoReset, onHit, shield — no armour aura in the description)

audit.whatIsWrong: The Granite Shield interaction is described loosely ('regenerates between poke trades') without the mechanic that makes Teemo uniquely good at suppressing it.
audit.why: Granite Shield only recharges once he has NOT been hit for a few seconds. Toxic Shot's poison ticks every second for four seconds after a single attack. One auto therefore holds his shield down for the whole poison duration — no other champion suppresses it this cheaply, and it is the reason a single auto is worth more here than a full trade.
audit.corrected: One Toxic Shot auto keeps Granite Shield suppressed for the full four seconds the poison ticks. Auto once, walk away, and it never comes back up.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (P: 'If Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds, this effect recharges')
champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (E Toxic Shot: 'dealing damage on impact and each second after for 4 seconds')

audit.whatIsWrong: 'mid' says that at levels 4-5 'Q is now max-ranked' and spikes[1] is titled 'Lvl 4-5' with 'With Q maxed'.
audit.why: Q rank 5 requires level 9. At level 5 it is rank 3. Teemo's Q cooldown is also flat 7s at every rank, so 'maxing' it never changes the trade rhythm the paragraph is built around.
audit.corrected: Rank 3 at best, on the same flat 7s cooldown it had at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Q cooldown '7' — one value for all ranks)

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers call Unstoppable Force 'undodgeable' / 'Un-dodgeable burst', and the full layer's cooldown entry instructs you to 'Blind + kite it'.
audit.why: Blind does nothing to an ability, so 'blind it' is impossible advice attached to the matchup's headline threat. The dangerous part is not the ultimate's own properties — it is that Seismic Shard has already taken your move speed when it arrives.
audit.corrected: You do not blind or kite Unstoppable Force. You avoid being slowed into it, and you use shrooms as the warning system on his approach paths.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart hands Teemo four of the last five stages and the prose says the lane 'tips comfortably your way' after first item. The packet shows 48.33% over 1947 games — Teemo loses this matchup, on the second-largest sample on the champion.
audit.why: This is the only genuinely losing matchup in my slice and it is written as a winning one. A Teemo who follows 'this lane tips comfortably your way' into the late game against a Malphite is walking into the ultimate the same guide calls undodgeable.
audit.corrected: Not flipping four chart stages unilaterally, but the direction is wrong against a very large sample and the late-game optimism should be pulled back to match. The missing Ground Slam interaction is the most likely reason the model over-rated Teemo's scaling here.

edits.before: Malphite's passive shield regenerates between poke trades — your E poison is the only way to drain it without walking into his W armor aura, so auto-then-back is your only safe pattern before you have Q.
edits.after: Granite Shield only recharges once he has gone a few seconds without being hit — and one Toxic Shot auto ticks poison for four straight seconds. Auto once, walk out, and his shield simply never comes back.

edits.before: With Q maxed you can blind him in the middle of his approach and deny the auto-stack he needs to run Thunderclap trades — this is your cleanest damage window before he stacks enough armor to feel your E.
edits.after: Q is rank 3 here, not maxed, and on the same flat 7s cooldown it always had. The real change is Ground Slam: 7s, 400 range, and it cuts the attack speed your entire poison engine runs on.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force is undodgeable and one-shots you: the instant he hits 6 treat him as a loaded gun — shroom the brushes around you and keep max range at all times or this lane ends in one button.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s and blind does nothing to it — but what kills you is Seismic Shard first, stealing your move speed for 3s from 625 range. Never eat the Q while his R is up.

edits.before: Land Blinding Shot before he auto-trades and immediately disengage with W before Unstoppable Force comes off cooldown
edits.after: Spend blind on the attacks Thunderclap loads, and stay outside 625 so Seismic Shard cannot take your speed

edits.before: Stack armor items like Iceborn Gauntlet to reduce your E poison's relative value and survive to level 6
edits.after: Stack armour — it does nothing against your magic poison, but it scales Ground Slam's damage directly

edits.before: Land Unstoppable Force on you even once — it ignores Blinding Shot entirely and the stun window kills you before W gets you out
edits.after: Land Seismic Shard first to steal your move speed for 3s, then Unstoppable Force into the window where you cannot walk away

edits.before: At level 2 his Thunderclap gives him a buffered auto trade that punches through your first blind window if you try to poke him in melee range — he wins direct trades until you can kite cleanly.
edits.after: At level 2 Thunderclap resets his attack and loads aftershocks into the next few — those are on-hit attacks, so blind is worth spending on them, but he still wins any trade you extend past one hit.

edits.before: Q maxed starts to genuinely drain his shield through the blind, but his armor stacking begins to blunt your E damage — the lane is a skill contest over who controls trade spacing.
edits.after: Ground Slam arrives and cuts your attack speed on a 7s cooldown, which is the one thing that actually stops your poison engine — his armour never touches the magic damage itself.

edits.before: With Q max and full poison stacks you dictate every trade: blind him, poison him, W out — he has no dash to answer and no CC to stop the disengage.
edits.after: Q at rank 3 and full poison stacks let you dictate the trades — but only from outside 625, where Seismic Shard cannot steal your speed.

edits.before: Malphite's passive Granite Shield regenerates fully when he hasn't taken damage for a few seconds, which makes your standard auto-poke loop dangerous: if you auto, E-poison, and retreat, his shield just resets between your windows. The correct pattern at levels 1-2 is to walk up, auto-cancel into E poison to apply the DoT, and immediately disengage with W — the poison ticks drain his shield while you are already out of his auto range, so by the time he regenerates it you have another E stack ready. Do not throw Blinding Shot at level 1 unless he is about to auto you for the first hit; save it so you can respond to his W Thunderclap all-in at level 2. He wins both of these first two levels on raw durability — his shield outheals your level-1 DPS, and at level 2 his W gives him bonus armor and a strong auto that punishes any trade you extend past one hit.
edits.after: Granite Shield recharges only when he has gone a few seconds without being hit, and Toxic Shot poison ticks every second for four seconds — so a single auto suppresses the shield for the entire poison duration. That is the whole early game: walk up, land one attack, apply the DoT, and leave. You do not need a trade; you need the poison clock running, and every second it runs is a second his shield is not coming back. Do not throw Blinding Dart at level 1 unless he is about to attack you — save it for Thunderclap at level 2, which resets his attack and loads aftershocks into the next few. Those aftershocks are on-hit attacks, which is exactly what blind erases, so one well-timed dart costs him the whole window rather than a single hit. He still wins both of the first two levels on raw durability, so bank the poison, take the CS, and refuse every trade you cannot end in one attack.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your cleanest window. Q is now max-ranked and your E poison is at full base damage — walk up, fire Blinding Shot into his face the moment he steps forward for a CS, poison him, and immediately W back. He cannot auto-trade through the blind and he has no dash to close the gap before Move Quick resets, so each poke cycle genuinely costs him HP with no rebuttal. Keep the wave slightly toward your side so he must leave tower range to farm, then plant mushrooms in the tribush and at the base of the ramp. The critical discipline here is never stepping past the wave toward him: his Seismic Shard Q slows you and keeps you in range for a follow-up, and if you are slowed when he hits level 6 you die. Play from the safe side of the wave at all times.
edits.after: Levels 4-5: Q is rank 3, not maxed, and its cooldown is a flat 7s at every rank, so nothing about your rhythm has actually changed. What changed is his — Ground Slam is a 7s cooldown at 400 range and it cuts your attack speed, which is the engine your entire damage output runs on. Extended trades belong to him now, short ones are still yours. Blind the attacks Thunderclap loads, poison him, and Move Quick straight back out before the second exchange. The discipline that matters most is the 625 line: Seismic Shard steals your move speed for three full seconds rather than merely slowing you, so he is faster while you are slower, and a Teemo without his speed when Malphite is level 6 is simply a dead Teemo. Play from the safe side of the wave and never contest a CS inside that range.

edits.before: - Malphite Unstoppable Force: matchup-defining — Un-dodgeable burst. Blind + kite it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Malphite Ground Slam 7s at 400: cuts your attack speed — the real matchup cooldown. - Seismic Shard 8s at 625: steals your speed for 3s and sets up his R. - Unstoppable Force 130/115/100: not blindable.

edits.before: Q-blind erases his auto-trade window entirely. Only take the trade when Malphite's Unstoppable Force is down.
edits.after: Q-blind eats the attacks Thunderclap loads. Trade in single hits — his Ground Slam owns anything longer.

edits.before: Un-dodgeable burst. Blind + kite it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Not blindable. Do not sit inside 625 with his Seismic Shard off cooldown.

edits.before: Malphite wastes Unstoppable Force — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Thunderclap's aftershocks are on-hit attacks — blind erases them.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Seismic Shard steals your speed for 3s — that is what lands it.

notes: MOST SIGNIFICANT GAP IN MY SLICE: Ground Slam (Malphite E) does not appear anywhere in either layer for this matchup — not once. It is a 7s flat cooldown that reduces attack speed, and Teemo's entire damage output is attack-speed-scaled on-hit poison, so it is the single ability that beats him. Its damage also scales off Malphite's own Armor, which means his defensive itemisation is offensive against Teemo — the exact opposite of the entry's claim that armour 'blunts your E damage' (it cannot; Toxic Shot is magic). I strongly suspect this omission is why the content chart rates Teemo as winning four of the last five stages in a matchup he loses at 48.33% over 1947 games. That chart needs redrawing after these corrections. TOOLING FLAGS on champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json for this pairing: (1) 'resistances-invalidated — Malphite bypasses stacking resistances (Granite Shield (P))' is a false positive; Granite Shield is a health-based shield and bypasses nothing. (2) 'knockup-enabler — Both sides carry displacement (Noxious Trap (R) vs Unstoppable Force (R))' is also a false positive on Teemo's half: Noxious Trap slows, it does not displace, and Teemo's kit file carries a knockup flag it does not earn. Same false flag drives the teemo-vs-kled knockup pairing. Champion-wide name defects still outstanding: "Blinding Shot" x271 and "Liandry's Angueur" x80 in champ-data/content/teemo.js.
